title: Practice Block Audit
summary: Diagnose lying blocks; rebuild an honest week.
checklist: List every block you claimed last week
Mark which ones produced a closeable artefact
Name the lie (length, time of day, or distraction)
Rebuild three honest blocks for next week
Protect one of them with a mix and a closed tab
body:
## What a lying block is

A lying block is a calendar rectangle that looks like practice and behaves like avoidance. It is two hours labelled *studio* that become plugin shopping, playlist rebuilding, or a conversation about the work that never becomes the work.

The audit is not moral. It is diagnostic. You are looking for a mismatch between **claimed minutes** and **closeable artefacts**.

## How to run the week in reverse

Take last week. For each claimed practice block, write one line: what exists now that did not exist before? A take. A verse. A patched cable. A sent invoice. If the line is empty, the block lied.

Most makers discover they have three honest hours hiding inside twelve theatrical ones.

## Rebuild rules

- Name the artefact before you start (*one verse demo*, *mix notes page*, *forty minutes of loops*).
- Time-box shorter than your pride wants. Honest forty beats fake two hours.
- Pair the block with a studio companion mix so the sonic room and the physical room agree.
- Close the tab that is not the work. Gear sites are not warm-ups.

## Mentor note

If you share a house, the honest block may be shorter than a video essay suggests. Design for Tuesday. Forgive the collapsed day. Tools can sit in a drawer overnight without becoming a referendum on your character.

## What this is not

Not a grind programme. Not a public streak. The only audience for the audit is you and, if you want, a collaborator who already knows your tells.

title: Finish Rates Over Inspiration
checklist: Define done for one current piece
Count finishes in the last 30 days
Pick a definition of done that is smaller
Schedule one close this week
Log it in a notebook, not a dashboard startup
body:
## Inspiration is a weather report

Weather is real. You do not build a practice on forecasts. Finish rate is the percentage of started pieces that reach a definition of done you wrote down in advance.

If you cannot say what *done* means, you cannot have a finish rate. You only have vibes.

## A boring definition of done

Examples that work: bounced stereo, sent to the collaborator, printed lyric with cuts, invoice paid, lesson plan in the folder. Examples that do not: *feels finished*, *would play for my heroes*, *ready for a poster about purpose*.

## Systems, not moods

- Keep a finish log with dates. Thirty days is enough to see a pattern.
- Shrink the definition until you can close something this week.
- Separate exploration sessions from closing sessions. Both are craft. They are not the same calendar rectangle.

## Mentor note

A high finish rate on tiny work beats a shrine to an unfinished epic. The epic can still exist. It just cannot be the only identity in the room.

title: Deep Work in the Studio
checklist: Choose one problem for the session
Set a mix that does not demand applause
Remove one input (second screen, chat, shop tab)
Work until the timer, then stop
Leave a one-line note for tomorrow
body:
## Attention is a studio resource

You already know this if you have ever lost a take to a notification. Deep work in a studio is not a Silicon Valley costume. It is session hygiene for ears and hands.

## Design the room

One problem, named. One mix that holds without shouting. One rectangle of desk. Headphones as the last physical act before the first sound.

Lyrics compete with language work. If you are writing, keep voices rare. If you are mixing, keep the playlist in another room.

## Stop on purpose

Stopping is part of the design. A session that melts into doomscrolling is not more dedicated. It is less designed.

Leave a note: *tomorrow, the second verse chorus join*. Future you should not have to reconstruct the weather.

title: The First Fifteen Minutes
checklist: Write a standing opener for this season
Use it for five sessions
Do not rebuild the opener each morning
Forgive the days you cannot have a door
Review whether it still reduces avoidance
body:
## Avoidance loves a blank session

The first fifteen minutes are where identity arguments happen (*am I a real musician today*). A standing opener removes the false problem so you can face the real one.

## Standing openers

Cable check and a known loop. One vocal siren. A page before screens. The point is familiarity, not novelty. Familiarity is a kind of mercy.

Rebuild the opener once a season, not every Tuesday.

## Mentor note

If you share space, the opener might be headphones and a closed door for twelve minutes. Practise the rule when you have it. Forgive yourself when you do not.

title: Session Hygiene
summary: A room clean enough to think.
checklist: Name the session file before you record
Coil one cable you always trip on
Clear one surface
Save with a version stamp
Leave the room kinder than you found it
body:
## Hygiene is attention

A studio that cannot be thought in will be shopped in. Hygiene is not aesthetics for a camera. It is the difference between a session and a shrine.

## Minimum viable tidy

One surface. One named version. One cable that no longer lies in wait. You do not need a warehouse system. You need Tuesday to survive.

## Version stamps

`song-v12-vocal-comp.wav` tells the truth. `finalFINAL2` is folklore. Manual v1.2 thinking belongs in audio too.

title: Versioning Without Chaos
checklist: Pick a stamp pattern and write it down
Apply it to one active project today
Archive, do not delete, two old versions
Tell collaborators the pattern
Stop renaming with feelings
body:
## Folklore versions hide work

If three people have three *finals*, you do not have a finish. You have a group project in denial.

## A pattern that is boring enough to keep

Date, increment, what changed. `2026-06-12-v07-mix-notes`. Share the pattern at the start of a collaboration, not after the fight.

## Mentor note

Archiving is kindness. Deleting to *keep it clean* is how you lose the only good verse from March.

title: Feedback Without Spiral
summary: A protocol for notes that does not eat the weekend.
checklist: Ask for one kind of note (mix, lyric, or arrangement)
Wait a walk before answering
Extract one actionable
Park identity comments
Schedule the tiny fix, not the personality rebuild
body:
## Spiral is optional

Feedback can be data. It can also be a story about whether you deserve to make things. The protocol exists so the story does not get the session.

## Ask smaller

*Is the chorus landing* is a better ask than *what do you think*. Specific questions get specific notes. Vague asks get identity.

## After the note

Walk. Then one actionable. If the note is chemistry or values, that is a collaborator conversation, not a 2 a.m. rewrite of the self.

Use the After Feedback mix if you need a sonic room that does not argue with you.

title: Shipping Week Checklist
checklist: Write the actual ship date
List assets that must exist (audio, art, one share)
Protect one practice block in the afternoon
Decide the metric freeze date
Plan the quiet after
body:
## Shipping is a week, not a personality

Countdown theatre is a funnel costume. A shipping week is a checklist: masters where they belong, art that is true, one share, then protect the afternoon so practice still happens.

## Metric freeze

Pick when you will look. Looking every hour is not marketing. It is a nervous system problem. Quiet releases are allowed. They still count as finishes.

## After

Log learnings. Rest. Next seed. The Post-Release Quiet mix exists so the spike does not become your only weather.

title: One-Page Career Map
summary: A map that fits a bag.
checklist: Write what you make in one sentence
Write who it is for in one sentence
List three current collaborators or rooms
Name one money floor
Name one next finish, not ten dreams
body:
## One page is the point

A career map that requires a slide deck is a stall. One page: what you make, who it is for, where it lives, what you will not do, the next finish.

Update it when the work changes, not when you feel behind.

## Not LinkedIn

This is not a personal brand canvas. It is a studio document. If it cannot travel in a bag to a session, it is too much.

Chemistry beats clout when the session gets hard. Put the people who have chemistry on the page.

title: Pricing the Work
checklist: Write a floor you will not go under
Write a fair rate for this season
Write a stretch for the work that costs you more
Practise one send sentence
Send one real number this month
body:
## Shrinking is a habit

Underpricing is often a nervous system move dressed as kindness. Kindness to collaborators includes a number they can plan around.

## Three scenarios

Floor: below this you decline or change the scope. Fair: what the work costs this year. Stretch: when the session asks more of your calendar or your ears.

Say the number. Send the invoice. Money Morning exists so this does not become a personality crisis.

## Mentor note

You can be generous with time and still have a floor. Generosity without a floor is often resentment later.

title: Collaborator Chemistry
summary: Green flags, red flags, and the hard session.
checklist: List three green flags you actually need
List three red flags you will not talk yourself out of
Write your boundary in one sentence
Use it on the next inquiry
Debrief one past session with honesty, not gossip
body:
## Chemistry beats clout

When the session gets hard — and it will — clout does not rack the cable. Chemistry does: shared pace, shared definition of done, shared respect for ears.

## Flags

Green: they show up, they name problems without contempt, they can hear no. Red: they move your finish line in public, they skip the opener, they treat your floor as a joke.

## Boundary sentence

Keep one you can say tired. *I can do two hours and a bounce; I cannot do an open-ended rewrite tonight.*

title: After a Quiet Release
summary: When the spike does not come, the work still happened.
checklist: Thank the people, not the graph
Log one learning
Rest without a revenge campaign
Plant a next seed smaller than your pride
Return to a practice block
body:
## Quiet is not failure

A quiet release can still be a finish. The industry story that every ship must spike is a poster. Posters are not maps.

## What to do

Thank. Log. Rest. Next seed. Do not build a second personality to punish the first.

If meaning matters to you, this is a place it can sit: the work was made; the day was honest. That is enough to return to the desk.

title: Purpose Without the Poster
summary: Calling as direction, not a slogan.
checklist: Write purpose as a direction for this season
Remove one hustle verb from your notes
Do one practice block that matches the direction
Leave the poster language off the homepage of your life
Revisit in a month, not every morning
body:
## Posters are not practice

Purpose language goes wrong when it becomes a campaign. *Calling*, here, means vocational direction: the kind of work you will protect time for. It is not an altar call and not a funnel.

## A seasonal sentence

*This season I finish songs with voices I trust.* That is a purpose you can schedule. *Unlock my potential* is not.

## Soft lean

If gratitude or stillness helps you keep the direction, you are welcome to it. If it does not, keep the desk. Purposetone is not a church site. Meaning is invited, not imposed.

title: Keeping Tone Under Pressure
summary: How you sound when the week is ugly.
checklist: Name one pressure that changes your tone
Write the tone you want under it
Pick a mix or walk that restores it
Practise one sentence you will not send angry
Review after the next hard session
body:
## Tone is a craft outcome

Keep your tone is not branding. It is how you speak in notes, in sessions, in invoices, when the week is ugly.

Pressure will try to make you a poster or a weapon. The work is to stay specific, kind, and direct.

## Under pressure

Shorter sentences. One problem. Walk before send. The Late Build mix exists so night finishing does not become a character test.

title: Stewardship of Attention
summary: Attention as a finite studio resource (soft lean).
checklist: Name your three attention thieves
Give one of them a closed-door hour
Protect one deep-work block this week
Notice where meaning helps you stop, not perform
Do not turn this chapter into a purity test
body:
## Attention can be stewarded

Stewardship here is not a sermon series. It is the old idea that some resources are finite and were never yours to burn for display.

Your attention is one of those resources. Feeds will take it. So will fear. So will a studio that is also a shop.

## Practice

Close a tab. Keep a mix stable for a month. Let Sunday be restoration if that is honest for you. If gratitude language is not yours, keep the sensory switch and move on.

This chapter is labelled with a soft lean on purpose. Skip it if you came for cables. It will still be here in June.

title: Rest as Part of Craft
checklist: Schedule one restoration day or half-day
Tell one person you will not ship that day
Use a mix that asks nothing
Notice the urge to earn rest
Return without a revenge practice binge
body:
## Rest is in the manual because makers skip it

If rest is only what happens when you collapse, it is not part of craft. It is an accident.

Restoration Day can include silence, a walk, one record, no output. Soft lean welcome: gratitude, stillness, a prayer-sized pause. Never required.

## Mentor note

Returning from rest without a binge is the skill. The work will still be there. Your tone might be better. That is the point.
